item.title: Surface corrections and vortex energetics in the Thomas--Fermi limit of a self-bound unitary Fermi superfluid
item.description: arXiv:2610.24565v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a spin-balanced unitary Fermi superfluid bound by an attractive $1/r$ interaction within an extended Thomas--Fermi density functional. Its large-particle-number limit is the Lane--Emden polytrope of index $3/2$. We prove the leading gradient correction to the ground-state energy and strong convergence of the density amplitude. A rescaled surface problem predicts the next energy correction and the leading integrated density error. Matching a vortex core to the polytropic bulk gives the energetic threshold of a singly quantized central vortex, including the constant beyond the leading logarithm. Linearizing the same surface problem predicts a local energetic threshold for collective surface excitations that, in the natural TF frequency units, decreases more slowly with particle number than the central-vortex threshold. Radial stationary, spherical Bogoliubov--Poisson, and axisymmetric real-time calculations test the predicted energy corrections and vortex matching, and resolve finite-size surface-mode minima whose approach to the continuum surface coefficient is followed to $N\simeq4\times10^6$. For the reference gradient coefficient the vortex constant is $c_1=-0.535$, and the surface Landau scale is $1.417\,\omega_K(\hbar_{\rm eff}^2/2R_{\rm TF})^{1/6}\propto N^{-1/9}$; sector energies at $N\simeq4.6\times10^5$, computed after the fit, agree with the extrapolated vortex threshold to $10^{-4}$. These results distinguish the accuracy of the Thomas--Fermi bulk from the gradient physics that controls the surface and vortex core, and separate vortex energetics from the open problem of nonlinear vortex entry.
item.dc:creator: Bao-Duy Le

item.title: Self-Trapping and Liouvillian Spectral Transitions in a Dissipative Bose-Hubbard Dimer
item.description: arXiv:2610.25222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the self-trapping transition in dissipative double wells using mean-field theory and exact diagonalization. We find that, similar to the conventional interaction-driven transition from oscillatory dynamics to self-trapping, dissipation alone can also induce self-trapping-like localization in one well. The resulting state, although transient and decaying, persists for a substantial time. At the mean-field level, the interaction- and dissipation-driven transitions are discontinuous and continuous, respectively. When interaction and dissipation both are present, their interplay produces three dynamical regimes: (i) at weak interaction, increasing dissipation drives a transition from oscillations to self-trapping; (ii) at moderate interaction, self-trapping at weak dissipation, oscillatory dynamics at intermediate dissipation, and re-entrant self-trapping at strong dissipation; and (iii) at strong interaction, self-trapping persists but is weakened by dissipation. We connect the transition with the Liouvillian spectrum. It is observed that purely dissipation-driven transition coincides with an exceptional point in the spectra, and a peak in the Liouvillian gap, marking the onset of the quantum-Zeno regime. In the presence of interactions, however, the onset of the Zeno regime is shifted to dissipation strengths larger than that required for the self-trapping transition.
item.dc:creator: Subhendu Saha, Raka Dasgupta

item.title: Near self-duality and spatial reorganization of anyon vortex lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.25412v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Contact attraction drives the self-generated vortex lattice of a trapped anyon gas towards self-duality, but integrated energies do not reveal where the remaining departure from it is located. We address this question in the almost-bosonic Chern--Simons--Schr\"odinger average-field model using a positive, gauge-invariant local defect that measures the covariant kinetic energy in excess of the magnetic bound. Numerically computed low-energy states at three statistical fluxes show that, as the stability line is approached, the integrated defect falls by about two orders of magnitude while the density modulation grows, so that magnetic saturation and density uniformity separate. The residual defect concentrates in a vortex-free outer shell that carries unscreened statistical flux. There it reduces to a smooth radial mismatch between the statistical flow and the density decay, which the interior lattice cannot cancel, whereas the covariant kinetic and amplitude-gradient energies show no comparable enrichment. The effect is robust to grid and box refinement, while its magnitude depends on flux and on the low-energy branch. Exact dilation and contact-response identities relate the squared energy to the density shape and provide consistency checks. Repulsion produces the opposite trend: a smoother density with a larger defect.
item.dc:creator: Bao-Duy Le

item.title: Two-Dimensional Quantum Droplets in a Mixture of Bose-Einstein Condensates
item.description: arXiv:2610.26449v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum droplets represent a striking manifestation of beyond-mean-field physics, with properties that depend sensitively on dimensionality. Although quantum droplets have been experimentally realized in one and three dimensions, their realization in two dimensions has remained elusive. Here, we observe the formation of a two-dimensional (2D) quantum droplet in a quasi-2D geometry by transferring the single-component Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) into a spin mixture in the Lee-Huang-Yang (LHY) regime, where the LHY effect evidently deviates from its three-dimensional form. We find that, in our scheme, 2D quantum droplets are more stable and exhibit longer lifetimes than previously reported quantum droplets. By instead transferring the initial BECs into another single-spin state with a negative scattering length, we generate 2D Townes solitons. A comparison between the two types of self-bound states shows that, whereas 2D Townes solitons are stable only near a critical atom number determined by the scattering length, 2D quantum droplets remain well-defined and self-bound over a much broader parameter range. These realizations of quantum droplets and Townes solitons in two dimensions provide new insights into self-bound states and open new avenues for exploring nonlinear dynamics in quantum liquids.
item.dc:creator: Yue Zhang, Liangchao Chen, Wei Han, Linshan Gong, Yazhou Wang, Zekui Wang, Xinhao Liang, Wenjie Sui, Pengjun Wang, Lianghui Huang, Zengming Meng, Zhuxiong Ye, Jing Zhang

item.title: Non-local Stabilization and Synchronization of Larmor Precession in Trapped Polariton Condensate Dimer
item.description: arXiv:2610.26499v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We demonstrate mutual synchronization of Larmor precessions between spatially separated, optically trapped polariton condensates. We identify the cross-condensate correlation g(2)1,2({\tau}) as a sensitive metric for condensate coupling. Synchronization of precessions in a condensate dimer is mediated by polariton outflow and resonantly depends on spectral overlap and precession winding. All-optical stirring of one site non-locally increases the pseudo-spin dephasing time of its static neighbor, prolonging phase-locking in a dimer by an order of magnitude. Our work establishes a scalable platform for studying non-equilibrium time-periodically driven systems and for high-speed spinoptronic networks.
item.dc:creator: Stepan Baryshev, Alexey Yulin, Ivan Gnusov, Sergey Alyatkin, Pavlos G. Lagoudakis

item.title: Exploring ground state phase diagrams of Rydberg atom arrays with finite projected entangled-pair states
item.description: arXiv:2610.26520v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Rydberg atom arrays (RAA) have been advocated as a promising avenue for the quantum simulation of different exotic quantum states. Numerical predictions for the ground state properties of this experimental platform can, however, be challenging in two-dimensional setups. In particular, faithfully treating long-range interactions is often crucial for distinguishing the fate of competing phases, but it usually comes at considerable cost. Projected entangled-pair states (PEPS), optimized via a sampling-based approach, have been shown to deal with such terms on the same ground as shorter-range ones. In this work, we employ these tools to investigate debated physical questions in different frustrated geometries of RAA, from the emergence of spin-glass physics on the Kagom\'e lattice to topological order beyond the PXP model on the Ruby lattice. By that, we contribute to establishing PEPS as well-suited tools for creating digital twins of RAA experiments.
item.dc:creator: Konrad Schr\"oder, Erik Lennart Weerda, Matteo Rizzi

item.title: Vortexable Chern Bands Sit Exactly on the Topological Floor of Flat-Band Superfluid Stiffness
item.description: arXiv:2610.24877v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vortexable Chern bands host ideal fractional Chern insulators. Paired with time-reversed partners by orbital-diagonal on-site attraction, they are the least stiff flat-band superconductors at fixed Chern number $C$, filling, and pairing amplitude. For uniform pairing and a nondegenerate paired state, the exact $T=0$ stiffness determinant is the topological floor times $1+(\Torb/2\pi|C|)^2\le1+(\TLVP/2\pi|C|)^2$, where $\Torb$ and $\TLVP$ measure departures from vortexability. Enhancement costs vortexability, and the inequality is strict only if internal components share a site, as in heterostrained bilayers.
item.dc:creator: Zhi-Wei Wang, Samuel L. Braunstein

item.title: Optical vortex bullets with large angular momenta
item.description: arXiv:2610.26289v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate three-dimensional spatiotemporal optical vortex solitons (light bullets with a toroidal shape) carrying higher-order orbital angular momentum in Kerr media with anomalous group-velocity dispersion and a transversely localized Gaussian profile of the linear refractive index. Stationary vortex bullets with topological charges (winding numbers) $1\leq \ell \leq 4$ are obtained as numerical solutions of the three-dimensional nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation, and their existence, structure and stability are systematically analyzed. In terms of atomic Bose-Einstein condensates, these solutions represent matter-wave solitons with embedded vorticity. We examine the dependence of the solution families on the propagation constant, the depth and width of the guiding profile, and $\ell $. It is found that the increase of $\ell $ requires one to use a stronger or wider waveguiding potential to sustain localized states satisfying the Vakhitov-Kolokolov (VK) stability criterion. VK-complying and non-complying branches of vortex-soliton families are separated by a degenerate Townes branch. Direct simulations reveal that, although the guiding profile substantially suppresses the collapse and extends the propagation distance of vortex bullets, their robustness is ultimately limited by azimuthal instabilities, whose growth is enhanced for values of $\ell $. These results demonstrate that engineered refractive-index landscapes significantly enlarge the stability domain of spatiotemporal vortex bullets and provide guidelines for supporting optical bullets carrying large orbital angular momenta.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'{e} R. Salgueiro, Carlos F. S\'{a}nchez, Boris A. Malomed, \'{A}ngel Paredes, Humberto Michinel

item.title: High-order resonances and emergent coherent dynamics in interacting Stark chains
item.description: arXiv:2610.26328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A linear potential gradient can strongly suppress quantum dynamics, while interactions can activate resonant many-body processes whose higher-order structure remains largely unexplored. Here we uncover a systematic hierarchy of high-order interaction--tilt resonances in an interacting Stark chain, where the resonance order counts the minimal number of elementary exchange steps involved. These resonances manifest as long-lived coherent oscillations with order-dependent timescales. By isolating individual resonant channels and developing a microscopic effective description, we connect these dynamical timescales to the underlying many-body exchange processes and reveal a pronounced dependence on the initial-state structure. Our results provide crucial insights into high-order many-body resonances and show how commensurate interaction-to-tilt ratios generate a hierarchy of parametrically slow coherent many-body dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Jiahe Chang, Hongzheng Zhao

item.title: End-to-End Optimization of Partial Fault Tolerance in Neutral-Atom Arrays
item.description: arXiv:2610.26471v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fault-tolerant (FT) quantum computation offers a pathway to quantum advantage, but its realization is hindered by its significant overhead. The partially FT "STAR" architecture reduces the cost of universal computation at the price of relaxing FT requirements for non-Clifford operations, increasing exposure to hardware noise. Therefore, maximizing its performance and applicability demands careful co-design with the underlying hardware. In this work we investigate the co-design of the STAR architecture with neutral-atom platforms, connecting the underlying atomic physics to logical error modeling and application-level performance. At the physical level, we identify a favorable noise bias in $^{171}\mathrm{Yb}$ Rydberg gates, and show how it can be enhanced through error-selective pulse optimization. At the logical level, we identify an intrinsic error suppression mechanism, yielding vanishing logical coherent noise in leading order. Detailed circuit-level simulations of surface code implementations show more than an order of magnitude reduction in logical error relative to previous estimates. As a concrete target application, we focus on the Fermi-Hubbard model with periodic boundaries, for which we design a simulation circuit particularly suited to early implementations. We quantify the resource tradeoff of partially and fully FT approaches to gate synthesis, with the former showing approximately an order of magnitude reduction in state-injection depth, and an even larger reduction in Clifford resources. Comparing with classical and fully FT approaches, we identify regimes where partial fault tolerance provides both lower overheads and lower error rates. In our estimates, this is accessible with moderate error rates $p\sim 10^{-3}$ and a few thousand qubits, underlining that for these types of problems, partial FT approaches provide a compelling pathway to early quantum advantage.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Veroni, Aydin Deger, Andrew J. Daley

item.title: Kolmogorov-type non-thermal fixed points and beyond of far-from-equilibrium dilute system: ultra-cold Fermi gas
item.description: arXiv:2508.18821v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The far-from-equilibrium dynamics driven by the scattering from next-to-leading-order (NLO) corrections in the quantum field theory has stationary solutions for the particle distribution characterized as the Kolmogorov-type non-thermal fixed points corresponding to scale-invariant particle/energy flux. The dynamics of the spatially homogeneous dilute ultra-cold Fermi gas is investigated, and its kinetic equation confirms the Kolmogorov-type non-thermal fixed points in the perturbation theory by the quasi-particle assumption, in contrast to the wave turbulence of the ultra-cold Bose gas. In addition, other stationary states are discussed when the the vertex correction becomes significant in the kinetic equation. It is found that conditions for the scale-invariant flux in this case no longer hold when the quasi-particle assumption is applied.
item.dc:creator: Chun-Wei Su

item.title: Nonlinear Landau levels in the almost-bosonic anyon gas
item.description: arXiv:2510.14679v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the quantitative description of a many-particle gas of interacting abelian anyons in the plane, confined in a trapping potential. If the anyons are modeled as bosons with a magnetic flux attachment, and if the total magnetic flux is small compared to the number of particles, then an average-field description becomes appropriate for the low-energy collective state of the gas. Namely, by means of a Hartree-Jastrow ansatz, we derive a two-parameter Chern-Simons-Schr\"odinger energy functional which extends the well-known Gross-Pitaevskii / nonlinear Schr\"odinger density functional theory to the magnetic (anyonic) self-interaction. One parameter determines the total number of self-generated magnetic flux units in the system, and the other the effective strength of spin-orbit self-interaction. This latter interaction can be either attractive/focusing or repulsive/defocusing, and depends both on the intrinsic spin-orbit interaction and the relative length scale of the flux profile of the anyons. Densities and energies of ground and excited states are studied analytically and numerically for a wide range of the parameters and align well with a sequence of exact nonlinear Landau levels describing Jackiw-Pi self-dual solitons. With increasing flux, counter-rotating vortices are formed, enhancing the stability of the gas against collapse. Apart from clarifying the relations between various different anyon models that have appeared in the literature, our analysis sheds new light on the many-anyon spectral problem, and also exemplifies a novel supersymmetry-breaking phenomenon.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Ataei, Ask Ellingsen, Filippa Getzner, Th\'eotime Girardot, Douglas Lundholm, Dinh-Thi Nguyen

item.title: Nonequilibrium quantum states emerging from flippable spins in random networks
item.description: arXiv:2505.11466v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recent advances in programmable quantum simulators have enabled the realization of irregular interaction networks, which natural crystal lattices cannot provide, together with time-resolved observation of quantum many-body dynamics. Understanding the nonequilibrium states that emerge from such networks has only just begun, and whether quantum many-body scar states can emerge in them remains open. Here, focusing on a quantum Ising spin system with random interaction networks under a weak transverse field, we introduce the flippability, the fraction of flippable spins, and present phenomenological laws that predict the emergence of quantum many-body scar states from the network structure. As the flippability increases, the Hilbert space becomes less fragmented. The largest kinetically accessible subspace shows nonintegrable level statistics, yet hosts a few eigenstates with abnormally low participation entropy, signalling scar states. Real-time dynamics from Fock states confirm these signatures: systems with higher flippability tend toward thermalization, whereas a few initial states show anomalously nonthermal dynamics. The flippability thus links the interaction-network structure of the Hamiltonian to nonequilibrium many-body dynamics without translational invariance, and may apply to other kinetically constrained quantum systems.
item.dc:creator: Yoshiaki Horiike, Yuki Kawaguchi

item.title: Electrostatic lens of a charged vortex
item.description: arXiv:2608.21490v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the local electrostatic response of a charged superfluid in the presence of a cylindrically symmetric vortex, allowing both the particle density and the thermodynamic compressibility to vary with the radial coordinate. Starting from the electrostatic charge response obtained from the phase-only Popov action, we introduce a local-density extension and derive the regular near-axis expansion of the scalar potential. The constant, quadratic, and quartic coefficients are obtained explicitly in terms of the local screening response and of the leading nonuniform contribution to the vortex density profile. For a three-dimensional unitary Fermi equation of state, the density dependence of the compressibility generates a definite thermodynamic contribution to the quartic coefficient. The resulting decomposition separates this equation-of-state contribution from the ordinary constant-screening and charge-source terms that occur at the same order. This provides a compact analytical connection between vortex-core thermodynamics and the local electrostatic profile of a charged superfluid.
item.dc:creator: Iogann Tolbatov, Luca Salasnich

item.title: Spin Chain with Continuous Exponential Symmetry: Topological Phase and Beyond
item.description: arXiv:2610.10682v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study symmetric gapped ground states of one-dimensional spin $S$ chains with a continuous exponential symmetry $U(1)\rtimes\mathbb Z_2$ with integer base $q$, where the U(1) charge has a modulated unit of charge $q^{L-j}$ decaying exponentially with site $j$. The simplest model is a quantum breakdown model that can be viewed as a $q$-deformation of the XXZ Haldane spin chain. We show that the topology of their symmetric ground states crucially depends on $S$ and $q$. For integer $S$, odd $q$ allows a nontrivial $\mathbb Z_2$ Haldane-type symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phase with protected edge modes, while even $q$ allows no nontrivial SPT phase. For half-odd integer $S$, odd $q$ prohibits any unique symmetric gapped ground state due to a Lieb-Schultz-Mattis obstruction, whereas even $q$ enforces a novel symmetric gapped phase which we name as the ``half-SPT" phase. Unconventionally, the half-SPT phase only has a symmetry protected edge mode on one edge, and has half of the string orders of an SPT phase. Our results uncover a new type of symmetry-protected gapped phases beyond existing classification schemes.
item.dc:creator: Biao Lian, Zhen Bi

item.title: Theory of exciton-exciton interactions with nontrivial electronic bands
item.description: arXiv:2610.13246v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Excitons are bound electron-hole pairs in semiconductors whose interactions influence optical properties and determine their collective behavior and emergent correlated phases. Despite the theoretical and experimental significance of these phenomena, a microscopic theory of exciton-exciton interactions that takes into account the full composite nature of these quasiparticles in systems with an arbitrary single-particle Hamiltonian is lacking. Here, we present a general theory of exciton-exciton interactions that builds upon our previous publication [Physical Review B 113, 155440 (2026)], which applied only to conventional semiconductors with weak band hybridization. By contrast, the theory presented here is valid in virtually any crystalline semiconducting system and can be applied to the study of biexciton formation and correlated excitonic phases in systems where band topology, quantum geometry, and moir\'e effects play a significant role. In addition to the analytical theory, we also present results in simple systems with flat bands with a nontrivial quantum metric and show that the biexcitonic spectrum differs strongly from that in the case without quantum geometry. Our theory paves the way for accurate quantitative calculations of biexciton spectra and excitonic many-body phases in modern condensed-matter systems.
item.dc:creator: L. Maisel Licer\'an, H. T. C. Stoof
